$comment: Copy deck for the Bob Johnson post-RO VSC campaign. Voice: DriveOne Red Bull register. Deadpan, cheeky, confident. No exclamation points. No em dashes or en dashes. Never call the DriveOne product a warranty.

campaign.name: Why Buy Now: post-service VSC campaign
campaign.audience: Bob Johnson service customers with a closed RO in the last 30 days and no vehicle service contract on file

emails.goal: Thank them for the visit, name the gap, hand them a free quote
emails.subject: {{first_name}}, one thing was missing from your file
emails.subjectAlt: Your {{vehicle_model}} is covered. You are not.
emails.preheader: No coverage on file. That is fixable in about four minutes, online, without talking to anybody.
emails.headline: Thanks for coming in. [[One line was blank.]]
emails.subhead: Your profile shows no vehicle service contract. You can still get one, and you can get it from us.
body: Your {{vehicle_year}} {{vehicle_model}} was in with us on {{last_ro_date}}. Everything on that ticket is handled.
Here is the part nobody mentioned in the service lane: there is no vehicle service contract attached to your file. Which means the next repair is priced at whatever the next repair happens to cost.
You do not have to buy that off a television commercial. You can buy it from the store that already knows the car.

featureRows.title: 0% payment plan, up to 36 months
featureRows.subtitle: No credit check. 5% down to start.

featureRows.title: Platinum, our best coverage
featureRows.subtitle: The top plan we offer, and the only one in this program. Exclusionary, not a stripped entry tier.

featureRows.title: {{deductible_home}} deductible at our store
featureRows.subtitle: Bring it back to {{dealer_short}} and your {{deductible_away}} deductible disappears. Roadside is included anywhere in the US.

emails.benefitStrip: Coverage is additive. The term and the miles are added on from the day you buy, on top of wherever the car is now. That is the lowest monthly we can do; longer terms and an unlimited mileage plan are on the quote page.
emails.ps: You do not need to call us, and you did not need to click anything to see your price. It is at the top of this email. The rest works online, on your schedule, with nobody on the other end of it.

emails.goal: Reframe the repair math without fear-mongering
emails.subject: That visit was the cheap one
emails.preheader: Modern cars are wonderful. Their parts are priced accordingly.
emails.headline: Today was the [[cheap]] one.
emails.subhead: Routine service is the small number. The large numbers live somewhere in the next few years.
body: Nothing about your {{vehicle_year}} {{vehicle_model}} is unusual. It is a normal car having a normal life.
Normal cars have alternators, and transmissions, and infotainment units that cost more than the first car you owned. Those parts do not fail on a schedule you get to see in advance.
A vehicle service contract is simply the decision to price that now, while the car is healthy, instead of later, when it is not.

featureRows.title: Covered repairs, covered parts and labor
featureRows.subtitle: You pay your deductible. We handle the rest of the conversation.

featureRows.title: Serviced right here
featureRows.subtitle: Same shop, same advisors, same people who already have your history.

featureRows.title: Term set at purchase
featureRows.subtitle: Match the coverage to how long you actually plan to keep the car.

emails.benefitStrip: Repair cost examples are verified and dated on request. We do not quote scary numbers we cannot source.
emails.ps: The quote is free and it does not put you on a list. There is no list.

emails.goal: Own the grievance: no call centers, no pressure, 100% online
emails.subject: Nobody is going to call you
emails.subjectAlt: This email has no salesperson attached to it
emails.preheader: That is not an oversight. That is the product.
emails.headline: Nobody is going to call you. [[That is the product.]]
emails.subhead: No hold music. No four step transfer. No representative standing by.
body: You already know what buying coverage usually feels like. Somebody reads a script. Somebody offers to check with a manager. Somebody calls back on a Tuesday.
We took all of that out. You open your quote, you pick a plan, you check out. The whole thing is online and it is yours to do at 11pm in a kitchen if that is when you have a spare four minutes.
If you would genuinely like to talk to a human at {{dealer_short}}, our service line is at the bottom of this email and they are good. But you will never need to use it to buy this.

featureRows.title: 100% online checkout
featureRows.subtitle: Quote, select, purchase. No appointment, no finance office.

featureRows.title: No pressure, no follow up call
featureRows.subtitle: We mean this literally. Nobody is assigned to chase you.

featureRows.title: 30 day full refund
featureRows.subtitle: Cancel in the first 30 days with no claims made and the full price comes back.

emails.benefitStrip: Open the quote. Close the tab. Come back in a week. It will still be there.
emails.ps: We are aware that an email telling you nobody will call you is itself a form of contact. We accept the irony.

emails.goal: The $0-at-our-store deductible, the strongest dealer-specific hook
emails.subject: Your deductible disappears when you come back
emails.subjectAlt: A number that goes to zero
emails.preheader: Bring the car back to {{dealer_short}} and the deductible on a covered repair goes away.
emails.headline: Come back to us and your deductible [[goes to zero.]]
emails.subhead: Anywhere else it is {{deductible_away}}. Here it is {{deductible_home}}.
body: Coverage bought through {{dealer_name}} carries a disappearing deductible. Take a covered repair to another authorized repair facility and you pay {{deductible_away}}. Bring it to us and you pay {{deductible_home}}.
This is not a loyalty points scheme. It is a line in the contract.
You are welcome to use any licensed repair facility the administrator authorizes, and the coverage travels with the car. We would just rather you did not have to.

featureRows.title: {{deductible_home}} deductible at {{dealer_short}}
featureRows.subtitle: On covered repairs, per your contract terms.

featureRows.title: Repairs anywhere the administrator authorizes
featureRows.subtitle: Breaking down out of town is a bad day, not a coverage problem.

featureRows.title: Your service history is already here
featureRows.subtitle: No starting from scratch with a shop that has never seen the car.

emails.benefitStrip: Same building. Same advisors. Smaller invoice.
emails.ps: Deductible terms are set by your contract. The quote page shows exactly which one applies to your vehicle before you buy.

emails.goal: Payment plan mechanics, remove the affordability objection
emails.subject: 0% for 36 months, no credit check
emails.preheader: 5% down. The rest spread out at zero percent. No credit pull.
emails.headline: Zero percent. [[Thirty six months.]] No credit check.
emails.subhead: The reason people skip coverage is almost never the coverage. It is the number on the day.
body: So we removed the number on the day. Coverage starts with 5% down. Whatever is left splits across up to 36 months at zero percent.
There is no credit check and there is no interest. It is a payment plan, not a loan, and it does not touch your credit file.

Your {{vehicle_model}} comes out at {{monthly_payment}} a month. That figure is at the top of this email, it is specific to your vehicle and mileage, and it is the same number you will see at checkout.

featureRows.title: 5% down to activate
featureRows.subtitle: {{down_payment}} down on your plan, then the monthly figure above.

featureRows.title: 0% for up to 36 months
featureRows.subtitle: No interest. Not a promotional rate that expires.

featureRows.title: No credit check
featureRows.subtitle: No hard pull, no soft pull, no effect on your score.

emails.benefitStrip: Payment plan. Not a loan. Not financing. The distinction matters and we keep it straight.
emails.ps: Pricing is set by vehicle, mileage and term. {{monthly_payment}} is your figure, not a range and not an average.

emails.goal: Educate on exclusionary vs listed-component, the real quality differentiator
emails.subject: The good kind of coverage has an ugly name
emails.preheader: Most plans list what is covered. Ours lists what is not. That gap is the whole game.
emails.headline: Platinum. [[Our best.]] Also the only one here.
emails.subhead: We sell one plan in this program and it is the top one. Exclusionary coverage, which is the good kind and has the worst name in the business.
body: A listed component plan names the parts it covers. If your part is not on the list, it is not covered, and the list is always shorter than the car.

An exclusionary plan flips it. It names the short list of things it does not cover, and everything else is in. You are reading a page instead of a phone book, and the burden sits with us rather than with you.
Exclusionary is the coverage level that usually costs extra elsewhere. Here it is the only one we sell, because Platinum is the only plan in this program.

featureRows.title: Platinum is the only plan here
featureRows.subtitle: Our highest tier. Not held back for a different customer, not upsold later.

featureRows.title: A short list of exclusions
featureRows.subtitle: Printed in the contract, readable before you buy. Term and mileage options, including unlimited mileage, are yours to pick.

featureRows.title: Transferable if you sell the car
featureRows.subtitle: Coverage follows a proper transfer to the next owner.

emails.benefitStrip: If you only remember one word from this campaign, it is this one.
emails.ps: The full terms and conditions are linked from the quote page. Read them. We wrote them to survive being read.

emails.goal: Differentiate from direct-response VSC telemarketers without naming anyone
emails.subject: We are not the people from the commercial
emails.subjectAlt: Your car's extended warranty, and other famous phone calls
emails.preheader: You have had that call. This is not that. We are the store that fixed your car.
emails.headline: We are not [[the people from the commercial.]]
emails.subhead: You have received the call about your vehicle's extended warranty. Possibly during dinner. Possibly twice.
body: Here is the difference, and it is not subtle. Those callers do not know your car. We have it in our system, with its service history, its mileage and the ticket we closed on {{last_ro_date}}.
We are not a call center that bought your number. We are the service department you drove to.

Coverage is administered by {{administrator}} and honored at any licensed repair facility they authorize. It is a real contract with a real obligor, sold by a store with a physical address you have parked at.

featureRows.title: A real administrator
featureRows.subtitle: {{administrator}} backs the contract.

featureRows.title: A real building
featureRows.subtitle: {{dealer_name}}, serving {{service_area}}.

featureRows.title: 24/7 roadside assistance included
featureRows.subtitle: Up to three events per year.

emails.benefitStrip: No robocall has ever known your mileage. We do.
emails.ps: If you would like to verify any of this in person, the service drive is open and we are exactly where you left us.

emails.goal: Ancillary benefits: roadside, towing, rental reimbursement
emails.subject: The parts of coverage nobody talks about
emails.subjectAlt: Roadside, rental, and the rest of it
emails.preheader: Coverage is not only for the day the transmission goes. Most of it is for smaller, more annoying days.
emails.headline: The big repair is [[not the only thing]] in here.
emails.subhead: Most of what you will actually use is the unglamorous middle of the contract.
body: Coverage gets sold on the catastrophic repair. In practice, the parts people use most are the small ones, and they work anywhere in the country rather than only in our zip code.
A tow on a Sunday night. A rental car while yours sits on a lift for three days. A sensor you had never heard of, which turns out to be essential.
None of that makes for dramatic advertising. All of it makes for a better Tuesday.

featureRows.title: 24/7 roadside assistance
featureRows.subtitle: Anywhere in the US, up to three events per year, towing included.

featureRows.title: Rental reimbursement
featureRows.subtitle: {{rental_rate}} per 6 hours of labor time, up to {{rental_max}} per claim visit.

featureRows.title: Towing to the nearest shop
featureRows.subtitle: Up to $100 per occurrence, part of the same roadside benefit.

emails.benefitStrip: Roadside covers three events a year. Most people use one and are glad it was there.
emails.ps: Rental reimbursement needs proof of rental submitted with an authorized claim, so keep the receipt. Benefit limits are set by your contract.

emails.goal: The honest why-buy-now: eligibility is mileage and age gated
emails.subject: Why we keep saying now
emails.preheader: Eligibility runs on mileage and model year. Both of yours are moving in one direction.
emails.headline: There is a window. [[Yours is open.]]
emails.subhead: We have avoided fake deadlines for eight emails. Here is the real one.
body: Vehicle service contracts are underwritten against mileage and model year. Every plan has a ceiling, and your {{vehicle_year}} {{vehicle_model}} showed {{vehicle_mileage}} miles at its last visit.

Nothing expires this Friday. No countdown clock is running. But coverage is additive: the term and the miles start the day you buy and get added to wherever the car is then. Every month you wait is a month of protection you are not holding, on a car that is quietly getting older.
Coverage cannot be bought retroactively. That is the entire reason this campaign exists.

featureRows.title: Priced on today's mileage
featureRows.subtitle: Your quote reflects {{vehicle_mileage}} miles today, and coverage is added from there.

featureRows.title: Some exclusions arrive with mileage
featureRows.subtitle: Seals and gaskets stop being covered once the car is past 125,000 miles at claim time.

featureRows.title: No coverage after the fact
featureRows.subtitle: Existing conditions are not covered by any contract, anywhere.

emails.benefitStrip: No countdown timer in this email. We checked.
emails.ps: If you have already sold or traded the {{vehicle_model}}, ignore all of this and enjoy the new one.

emails.goal: Graceful close, permission-respecting, leaves the door open
emails.subject: Last one from us on this
emails.subjectAlt: We are going to stop emailing you about this
emails.preheader: Ten emails is a reasonable limit. Your quote link stays alive regardless.
emails.headline: This is the last one. [[Genuinely.]]
emails.subhead: We said there would be no pressure, and a campaign that never ends is pressure.
body: You have now received ten emails about vehicle service contracts. That is enough emails about vehicle service contracts.
Your quote stays live and your link keeps working. If the {{vehicle_model}} makes a sound you do not like in March, it will be there.
Either way, thank you for servicing with {{dealer_name}}. That part we would like to keep doing.

featureRows.title: Your quote link stays active
featureRows.subtitle: Bookmark it. Use it whenever.

featureRows.title: We will still service the car
featureRows.subtitle: Coverage or no coverage, nothing changes in the drive.

featureRows.title: No further emails in this series
featureRows.subtitle: This sequence ends here automatically.

emails.benefitStrip: No hard sell on the way out. That would undercut the previous nine emails.
emails.ps: If you would rather hear nothing from us at all, the unsubscribe link below works instantly and we will not make you explain yourself.
